channel.title: Trend Reader
channel.description: The AI vocabulary, mapped: a weekly brief on the terms and themes to know, and every new term as it is defined.

item.title: Weekly brief, week W40: Benchmark scores are losing their standing as a single number
item.description: This week's terms: none new. Themes: Benchmark scores are losing their standing as a single number; Containment failures are surfacing faster than the disclosure record can keep pace; Recursive self-improvement is moving from research demonstration to production tooling; Frontier pricing keeps falling while the inputs behind it get pricier.

item.title: New term: Claude Opus 5.5
item.description: Claude Opus 5.5 is Anthropic's first Claude 5.5 model, released on 22 September 2026 at $4 and $20 per million tokens with cache reads cut 60 percent, the first price cut in the Opus line's history. It matters because Anthropic claims Fable 5.1-level quality at 40 percent lower cost, which reset the price of frontier-grade capability in the same week as OpenAI's GPT-6 Sol and Luna.

item.title: New term: GPT-6 Luna
item.description: GPT-6 Luna is the cheapest tier of OpenAI's GPT-6 family, released on 22 September 2026 at $0.10 per million input tokens and $0.50 per million output tokens, a price OpenAI states is permanent. It matters because it puts near-frontier coding ability within reach of free-tier users and high-volume workloads at a fraction of Astra's cost per task.

item.title: New term: SGLang
item.description: SGLang is an open-source serving engine for large language models, used both as a production inference runtime and as the reference stack that published serving benchmarks are measured on. It matters because the engine, not only the accelerator, decides throughput and cost per token, and an open engine makes those numbers comparable across hardware.

item.title: Weekly brief, week W39: Price of the frontier resets, but the bill is set by effort and cache
item.description: This week's terms: Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6 Luna. Themes: Price of the frontier resets, but the bill is set by effort and cache; The harness is now measured, priced and trained; The score belongs partly to the scaffolding; Self-improvement claims moved from the model to its inputs; Agent load rotates the scarce input and pushes containment into the platform.

item.title: Weekly brief, week W39: The unit of competition is the system around the model
item.description: This week's terms: none new. Themes: The unit of competition is the system around the model; Two markets, tokens and revenue; Output per scarce input is the unit; The safety story matured to a governance floor; Benchmarks: measurement quality, not direction.
